opp_001:n1.prompt:
You are helping me complete the first step of sending an outgoing wire or ACH payment: collecting and validating the payee details and amount before the payment enters our approval gate. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for any of the following you don't already have: payee legal name, payee bank name, payee account number, routing number (for ACH) or SWIFT/BIC and intermediary bank info (for wire), payee address, payment amount, currency, payment method (wire or ACH), purpose/memo, and any supporting reference (invoice number, contract, or PO).
2. Once collected, format all of this into a single clean payment request record (plain text or table) with every field labeled clearly, so it can be handed to whoever approves and executes the payment from our bank account.
3. Sanity-check the data: confirm the routing number is 9 digits, flag if SWIFT/BIC looks malformed, flag if amount or currency fields are missing or ambiguous, and note any mismatch between payee name and account details if I've given you prior records to compare against.
4. Do not initiate or submit the payment yourself, and do not attempt to contact the payee's bank — this step is only about gathering and organizing the payment details for the approval step that follows.
5. Report back with the completed payment request record, a short list of any fields still missing or flagged for my confirmation, and a one-line summary (payee, amount, currency, method) I can quickly review before it moves to approval.

If I give you incomplete or conflicting information, ask clarifying questions rather than guessing. Keep the final record ready to paste directly into our approval workflow.

opp_001:n2.prompt:
You are helping me initiate a wire or ACH payment in {{vendor}}, our startup banking platform, so it sits pending approval before any funds move. Before starting, ask me for whatever is missing: (1) which {{vendor}} account/workspace to use, (2) payment type (wire or ACH), (3) recipient details (name, bank account/routing info or saved payee), (4) amount and currency, (5) memo/invoice reference, and (6) the desired send date. Use my configured credentials to access {{vendor}} via its dashboard or documented API.

Actions to take:
1. Confirm the recipient is set up correctly in {{vendor}} (existing payee or new one needs adding).
2. Create the payment request (wire or ACH) for the specified amount and recipient, making sure it is created in a pending/approval-required state — do not mark it as approved or sent.
3. Retrieve and show me the delivery estimate (expected arrival date/time and any fees) that {{vendor}} displays before confirmation.
4. Verify the payment is routed into our approval workflow and identify who is the designated approver.
5. Prepare a clear summary: recipient, amount, payment type, memo, delivery estimate, and current status (pending approval).

What done looks like: the payment request exists in {{vendor}} in a pending-approval state, with an accurate delivery estimate captured, and no money has moved.

Important: this step requires human approval before the payment is sent. Do not approve, authorize, or submit the payment yourself under any circumstance — prepare everything and then stop for human sign-off, reporting back the pending payment details, delivery estimate, and who needs to approve it.

opp_001:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare (but not execute) the release of a pending wire or ACH payment in our company's online banking dashboard, which sits behind a dual-control approval gate. This is the final financial-control checkpoint and must be authorized by an accountable human — releasing the payment remains a human step and you must never click 'release,' 'approve,' or 'authorize' on my behalf.

Please do the following preparation work:

1. Ask me for any missing details: the bank name/dashboard I use, the payment ID or reference number, payee name, amount, payment type (wire or ACH), and the intended send date.
2. If you have read access to the banking dashboard or transaction export, retrieve and summarize the pending payment's details (payee, account last-4 if visible, amount, date created, initiator name, current approval status) so I can verify them before release.
3. Cross-check the payment details against any supporting documentation I provide (invoice, contract, approved payment request) and flag any mismatches in amount, payee name, or account number.
4. Prepare a concise release checklist covering: correct payee verified, amount matches approved request, no duplicate payment exists, sufficient account balance, and correct payment date.
5. Draft a short confirmation note I can post internally (e.g., to finance Slack or email) once released, documenting who approved it and when.

Do not log into the banking dashboard to click release, do not approve or authorize the transaction, and do not submit any confirmation on my behalf — stop for human sign-off once the checklist and verification summary are ready.

Report back with: the verified payment details, any discrepancies found, the completed pre-release checklist, and the drafted internal confirmation note, clearly stating that the actual release action is pending my manual approval in the banking dashboard.

opp_001:n4.prompt:
You are helping me confirm that a wire or ACH payment I initiated from our company bank account has actually posted and settled, and reconcile it in our books. This is an async step: the settlement result may not be available immediately, so you should check now and be prepared to poll again later if the payment is still pending.

If you don't already have it, ask me for: the {{vendor}} account/login access details (assume I have configured credentials for you to use), the payment reference or transaction ID, the expected amount, and the expected settlement date.

Using our {{vendor}} banking platform, please:
1. Look up the specific wire/ACH transaction by reference ID or amount/date in the transaction list or activity feed.
2. Check whether it shows as posted/settled, and if {{vendor}} provides a delivery estimate, note whether we're still within that window or overdue.
3. Cross-check the account's balance history or ledger to confirm the debit matches the expected amount and date.
4. Pull the transaction details needed for reconciliation (date, amount, counterparty, memo/reference) so they can be matched against our accounting records or synced automatically if {{vendor}} offers accounting/ERP sync.
5. If the payment is still pending or not yet visible, note that and flag it for a follow-up check rather than treating it as failed.

Done looks like: you've confirmed settlement status (settled, pending, or failed) with supporting details (date, amount, reference), and either reconciled it against our accounting records or clearly flagged what still needs manual matching.

Report back with: the transaction status, key details you found, whether reconciliation is complete or needs another poll, and any discrepancies (amount mismatch, delay beyond estimate, etc.) that need my attention.
